correctness.rationale: For each integer \(m\ge2\), \(k\ge3\), the graph and projectors are well-defined and symmetric. The derivation uses a proved clique/star Laplacian separation and explicitly invertible star Green matrix, checks all absolute-value signs, and exhausts three edge-orbit types. Exact symbolic simplification of comparison polynomials proves every winner and tie. A standalone grounded-Laplacian checker reproduces all 406 actual projector columns on nine parameter pairs as corroboration, not an infinite proof.

evidence: General Green-operator or transfer-current representations apply to all finite graphs and express the projector matrix as an incidence-Laplacian pseudoinverse product.

The related discrete torus/Hamming computations in arXiv:2305.12582 concern other graph families; the star factor is irregular, and their homogeneous spectral formulas do not automatically yield the exact switching law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A graph-general projector identity covers how to calculate matrices but does not cover sharp closed endpoint norm formulas and maximizing directions on this particular family. None of the inspected stronger statements implies the two sign polynomials or their complete integer classification without new graph-specific work.

Searched research records and inspected primary work on cycle projections, Hamming graphs, tori and finite Lipschitz-free graph quotients did not supply a logically stronger or equivalent formula.
